audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction of the matchup was never stated, and the ability that carries it was named wrong. spikes[0] and wants.you[1] called her lane hop 'Between Worlds' — that is her ultimate. The hop is Across the Veil (W). spikes[1] also credited her ultimate with 'a damage-reduction shield', which is not in her kit.
audit.why: Riot text: Across the Veil (W, 22/21/20/19/18s, 700) 'leaps in a direction... becoming invisible'; Between Worlds (R, 140/120/100s, 250) 'leaps... releasing a shockwave... creates an area that slows... and allows Aurora to teleport from one side to the other'. No shield anywhere. Both W and R carry the dash flag, and Miasma's Riot text is explicit: 'Grounded enemies cannot use Movement abilities' — so your W shuts both of them off.
audit.corrected: Names fixed, the fabricated shield removed, and Miasma-grounds-both-leaps written into phases[1].why, phases[4].why, dontsFull[1].d, spikes[0], spikes[1], ahead and breakdown.carry.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held no digit, dosFull[2].d invented a 'fifteen-second' hop, and late described her mobility as 'limited charges' — she has none.
audit.why: Across the Veil 22s at rank 1 down to 18s, Twofold Hex 9s, The Weirding 15s, Between Worlds 140s at rank 1 against your 120s Gaze — you get the first ultimate.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, winCon, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d, spikes[0], spikes[1] and late.

audit.why: Both layers already read Skill, Skill, Skill, Cassiopeia, Skill, Cassiopeia, Cassiopeia with no disagreement, the packet lists no chart defect, and 49.51% over 412 games supports a near-even chart. The whys were left in place; only the fabrications around them were fixed.

edits.before: With items online, Cassiopeia's sustained ranged damage and zone denial clearly outclass Aurora's hit-and-run kit — her dashes have limited charges and cooldowns, so in extended fights your DPS simply outlasts her poke-and-reposition game plan. She's forced into pick-and-retreat mode rather than straight duels.

notes: Chart left untouched: both layers already agreed on all seven rows and the packet lists no chart defect. Aurora's W is described by Riot as making her invisible on landing — whether that is true invisibility or camouflage, and whether it breaks on damage, is not in the text, so nothing was asserted about revealing her. Whether Between Worlds' teleport across its own zone still works while grounded is likewise unstated; spikes[1] only claims the initial leap is groundable, which the dash flag supports.
